title: Does Shallow Alignment Extend to Multimodal Models? Probing Vision-Language Safety Depth

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: test whether multimodal training shallows or deepens alignment, with implications for deployment risk. However, the link between VLM-specific alignment depth and actionable defense is less direct than the text-only version.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running VLMs (LLaVA, MiniGPT-4) which are large and memory-intensive. Generating adversarial images and comparing against text-only baselines adds substantial complexity. Beginners would struggle with the multimodal pipeline setup even with mentor guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple interacting dimensions: text prefilling attacks on VLMs, adversarial image generation, cross-modal comparison. No clear single first deliverable; the comparison across text-only and multimodal requires completing two separate experimental setups.

novelty.reasoning: While VLM jailbreak attacks are heavily studied (JailBound 2025, multi-modal linkage attacks, split-image attacks, SPA-VL CVPR 2025), the specific framing of 'shallow alignment depth' applied to multimodal models is not yet directly addressed. Existing work covers VLM safety alignment broadly and identifies the modality gap as a vulnerability, but does not systematically measure alignment depth (token-level) in VLMs the way Qi et al. did for text-only models. However, the general finding that VLM safety is fragile is well-established.

evidence: JailBound: Jailbreaking Internal Safety Boundaries of Vision-Language Models. arXiv:2505.19610, 2025.
SPA-VL: A Comprehensive Safety Preference Alignment Dataset for Vision Language Models. CVPR 2025.
Jailbreak Large Vision-Language Models Through Multi-Modal Linkage. arXiv:2412.00473, 2024.
